profile.feeling: Golden curries, yellow-stained fingers and fashionable health drinks.

senses.def: turmeric (Curcuma longa): the plant and its orange-yellow rhizome, fresh or dried and ground
(as a colour word) ginger-yellow, ginger-coloured

examples.text: 咖喱的黄色主要来自姜黄。
examples.tr: The yellow colour of curry comes mainly from turmeric.
examples.py: Gālí de huángsè zhǔyào láizì jiānghuáng.

examples.text: 新鲜姜黄的样子像姜，切开以后是橙黄色的。
examples.tr: Fresh turmeric looks like ginger; cut open, it is orange-yellow inside.
examples.py: Xīnxiān jiānghuáng de yàngzi xiàng jiāng, qiēkāi yǐhòu shì chénghuángsè de.

examples.text: 印度菜常常用姜黄。
examples.tr: Indian dishes often use turmeric.
examples.py: Yìndù cài chángcháng yòng jiānghuáng.

examples.text: 姜黄粉要少放，放多了菜会发苦。
examples.tr: Use ground turmeric sparingly — too much makes a dish bitter.
examples.py: Jiānghuáng fěn yào shǎo fàng, fàng duō le cài huì fā kǔ.

collocations.tr: curcumin, the yellow pigment of turmeric

synonyms.nuance: ‘yellow ginger’: the name in Cantonese and in Hokkien (Penang, Singapore)

etymology.text: 姜 (‘ginger’) + 黄 (‘yellow’): the ‘yellow ginger’ — turmeric belongs to the ginger family; the traditional form 薑黃 keeps the ginger character 薑.

funFacts: The scientific name Curcuma comes from Arabic كُرْكُم (kurkum); German Kurkuma and Hebrew כּוּרְכּוּם (kurkum) carry the same word.
Curcumin (姜黄素), the yellow pigment, is the food colouring E100.
pitfalls: 姜黄 is not ginger (姜): same family, but turmeric is earthy and bitter and stains everything yellow.
As a colour word 姜黄 means ginger-yellow (Wiktionary also lists it as an adjective).
subtleties: In a Chinese kitchen it is mostly met as 姜黄粉 (the powder); fresh 姜黄 is sold in the south and in Southeast Asian shops.

ref.src: CC-CEDICT (MDBG): 琉璃苣 liu2 li2 ju4 ‘borage’; zh.wikipedia (Wikidata Q147075); Wiktionary has no entry

profile.feeling: Starry blue flowers in a European herb garden.

senses.def: borage (Borago officinalis): a herb with hairy leaves and blue star-shaped flowers, both edible

examples.text: 琉璃苣开蓝色的小花，像星星一样。
examples.tr: Borage has small blue flowers, like stars.
examples.py: Liúlíjù kāi lánsè de xiǎo huā, xiàng xīngxing yíyàng.

examples.text: 琉璃苣的叶子有黄瓜的味道。
examples.tr: Borage leaves taste of cucumber.
examples.py: Liúlíjù de yèzi yǒu huángguā de wèidao.

examples.text: 德国法兰克福的绿酱里有琉璃苣。
examples.tr: The green sauce of Frankfurt in Germany contains borage.
examples.py: Déguó Fǎlánkèfú de lǜ jiàng li yǒu liúlíjù.

profile.synonymsNone: No other everyday name: borage is a garden herb in China, known by this one name from gardening books and Western recipes.

etymology.text: 琉璃 (‘coloured glaze, glass’) + 苣 (a lettuce-type leaf vegetable, as in 莴苣); the name evokes the glassy blue flowers.

funFacts: German calls borage Borretsch or Gurkenkraut, ‘cucumber herb’ — after the same cucumber taste.
The blue flowers are edible and are frozen into ice cubes or scattered on salads.
pitfalls: 苣 is jù here, as in 莴苣 (wōjù); only in 苣荬菜 (qǔmǎicài, sow thistle) is it read qǔ.
subtleties: Not a market vegetable in China: you will meet the word in seed catalogues, herb gardens and translated recipes.

override.meaning: Wiktionary glosses 藜 only as “goosefoot” (and the surname Li). In Chinese botany 藜 is Chenopodium album, fat hen / lamb’s quarters: zh.wikipedia title for Wikidata Q158610, and CC-CEDICT “fat hen, goosefoot … Chenopodium album”.

profile.feeling: A dusty-grey wild green from the field edge; bookish as a single character.

senses.def: fat hen, lamb’s quarters (Chenopodium album): a wild goosefoot whose young leaves are eaten
goosefoot plants (Chenopodium) in general
Li, a surname

examples.text: 藜的嫩叶可以凉拌，也可以做包子馅。
examples.tr: Young fat-hen leaves can be dressed cold or used as a bun filling.
examples.py: Lí de nèn yè kěyǐ liángbàn, yě kěyǐ zuò bāozi xiàn.

examples.text: 春天，田边长满了藜，农民叫它灰灰菜。
examples.tr: In spring the field edges are full of fat hen; farmers call it huihuicai.
examples.py: Chūntiān, tián biān zhǎngmǎn le lí, nóngmín jiào tā huīhuīcài.

examples.text: 藜麦和藜是亲戚，原产南美。
examples.tr: Quinoa is a relative of fat hen; it comes from South America.
examples.py: Límài hé lí shì qīnqi, yuánchǎn Nánměi.

collocations.tr: (literary) goosefoot and bean leaves: the coarse food of the poor
(literary) a walking stick made from a goosefoot stalk

synonyms.nuance: the everyday northern name when it is picked and eaten; 灰 ‘grey’ after the powdery leaves
the same with a reduplicated, homely ring; widespread in the countryside

etymology.text: Phono-semantic character: 艹 (‘plant’) + phonetic 黎 (lí).

funFacts: Quinoa is 藜麦 in Chinese — ‘goosefoot grain’ — because it is a Chenopodium like fat hen.
English ‘goosefoot’ and German Gänsefuß (fat hen is Weißer Gänsefuß) both describe the leaf shape.
pitfalls: 藜 lí is not 梨 lí (pear) or 黎 lí (dawn; the Li people) — same sound, different characters.
Alone, 藜 sounds botanical or literary; when people pick and cook it they usually say 灰菜 or 灰灰菜.
subtleties: The young leaves look dusted with white-grey powder — that is the 灰 ‘grey’ of its everyday names.

profile.feeling: Earthy, woody sticks in Japanese and Taiwanese kitchens; health teas.

senses.def: burdock (Arctium lappa); above all its long root, eaten as a vegetable (Japanese gobō)

examples.text: 牛蒡削皮以后要泡在水里，不然会变黑。
examples.tr: Once peeled, burdock must go into water, or it turns dark.
examples.py: Niúbàng xiāopí yǐhòu yào pào zài shuǐ li, bùrán huì biàn hēi.

examples.text: 牛蒡茶在日本和台湾很受欢迎。
examples.tr: Burdock tea is popular in Japan and Taiwan.
examples.py: Niúbàng chá zài Rìběn hé Táiwān hěn shòu huānyíng.

examples.text: 牛蒡的根可以长到一米左右。
examples.tr: A burdock root can grow to about a metre long.
examples.py: Niúbàng de gēn kěyǐ zhǎng dào yì mǐ zuǒyòu.

synonyms.nuance: Taiwanese Hokkien nickname, ‘love-your-wife vegetable’ (某 = wife in Hokkien)

etymology.text: 牛 (‘ox’) + 蒡 (bàng, a character used almost only in this word). Wiktionary: possibly because oxen were seen eating its leaves when recovering from illness.

funFacts: Velcro was invented by George de Mestral after he studied the burdock burrs caught in his dog’s fur.
Japan is where burdock became an everyday vegetable (gobō); in China it is mostly a health food and a medicine.
pitfalls: 蒡 is bàng (4th tone), not páng — 旁 is only the sound hint inside it.
subtleties: In Chinese medicine the part used is the seed, 牛蒡子; as food it is the root.

profile.feeling: Sushi bars, green heat rushing up the nose, tears.

senses.def: wasabi (Eutrema japonicum): the plant and its rhizome, grated fresh

examples.text: 真正的山葵很贵，要现磨现吃。
examples.tr: Real wasabi is expensive and is grated just before eating.
examples.py: Zhēnzhèng de shānkuí hěn guì, yào xiàn mó xiàn chī.

examples.text: 很多寿司店的“芥末”其实不是山葵，而是辣根。
examples.tr: In many sushi bars the “wasabi” isn’t wasabi at all but horseradish.
examples.py: Hěn duō shòusī diàn de “jièmo” qíshí bú shì shānkuí, ér shì làgēn.

examples.text: 山葵喜欢长在清凉的溪水边。
examples.tr: Wasabi likes to grow beside cool streams.
examples.py: Shānkuí xǐhuan zhǎng zài qīngliáng de xīshuǐ biān.

synonyms.nuance: the everyday word for the green paste served with sushi — strictly ‘mustard’, and usually made from horseradish
‘green mustard-heat’: the usual name in Cantonese menus
a sound loan of Japanese wasabi, through Taiwanese Hokkien

etymology.text: Orthographic borrowing from Japanese 山葵 (wasabi): the Japanese spelling read the Chinese way, shān ‘mountain’ + kuí.

funFacts: Wasabi, horseradish (辣根) and mustard (芥菜) all belong to the cabbage family.
Fresh wasabi loses its sharpness soon after grating, which is why it is grated at the table.
pitfalls: 芥末 is not 山葵: 芥末 is strictly mustard, and the green “wasabi” paste is mostly horseradish with colouring.
subtleties: 葵 alone was an ancient leaf vegetable (a mallow) and is now mostly the sunflower (向日葵); in 山葵 it is just part of a borrowed Japanese spelling.

profile.feeling: North China: winter stacks of scallions, Shandong pancakes, Peking duck.

senses.def: Welsh onion (Allium fistulosum), especially the big, long-stalked northern type with a long white shaft
(Singapore Hokkien, Teochew) onion

examples.text: 山东大葱又长又甜。
examples.tr: Shandong scallions are long and sweet.
examples.py: Shāndōng dàcōng yòu cháng yòu tián.

examples.text: 煎饼卷大葱是山东的家常吃法。
examples.tr: A pancake rolled around a scallion is a Shandong home favourite.
examples.py: Jiānbing juǎn dàcōng shì Shāndōng de jiācháng chīfǎ.

examples.text: 北京烤鸭要配大葱丝和甜面酱。
examples.tr: Peking duck comes with shredded scallion and sweet bean sauce.
examples.py: Běijīng kǎoyā yào pèi dàcōng sī hé tiánmiànjiàng.

examples.text: 我买一根大葱。
examples.tr: I’ll buy a stalk of Welsh onion.
examples.py: Wǒ mǎi yì gēn dàcōng.

collocations.tr: raw scallion dipped in bean sauce (a northern dish)
the famous giant scallions of Zhangqiu, Shandong

synonyms.nuance: the general word: the species itself; 大葱 is its big northern type, 小葱 the thin one
‘Beijing scallion’: the name on Cantonese menus

etymology.text: 大 (‘big’) + 葱 (‘scallion’). 葱 (traditional 蔥) is inherited from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *b-tsoŋ ‘onion’, cognate with Tibetan བཙོང (btsong).

funFacts: The ‘Welsh’ in English Welsh onion has nothing to do with Wales: it is usually explained from Old English welisc ‘foreign’.
Japanese negi (ネギ) is the same species.
pitfalls: In Singapore Hokkien and Teochew, 大葱 means the round onion (洋葱) — Wiktionary.
葱 cōng (1st tone) sounds exactly like 聪 cōng ‘clever’; don’t mix up the characters.
subtleties: With 大葱 the white shaft (葱白) is the prized part; with 小葱 people mostly use the chopped green (葱花).

profile.feeling: Sour pink stalks in European gardens; a bitter yellow medicine in China.

senses.def: rhubarb (Rheum), including garden rhubarb, whose sour leaf stalks are cooked like fruit
rhubarb root and rhizome as a drug in Chinese medicine (a strong laxative)

examples.text: 欧洲人用大黄的茎做果酱和派。
examples.tr: Europeans make jam and pies from rhubarb stalks.
examples.py: Ōuzhōu rén yòng dàhuáng de jīng zuò guǒjiàng hé pài.

examples.text: 大黄的叶子有毒，不能吃。
examples.tr: Rhubarb leaves are poisonous — don’t eat them.
examples.py: Dàhuáng de yèzi yǒu dú, bù néng chī.

examples.text: 中医用大黄来通便。
examples.tr: Chinese medicine uses rhubarb root as a laxative.
examples.py: Zhōngyī yòng dàhuáng lái tōngbiàn.

synonyms.nuance: ‘edible rhubarb’: the precise name of the vegetable, as opposed to the medicinal species

etymology.text: 大 (‘big’) + 黄 (‘yellow’): ‘big yellow’, traditionally explained by the large yellow root used in medicine.

funFacts: Chinese rhubarb root travelled the Silk Road as a medicine; Europe imported it long before it started eating the stalks.
English rhubarb and German Rhabarber come from Medieval Latin rha barbarum, ‘foreign rha’.
pitfalls: In Chinese, 大黄 first suggests the medicinal root; say 食用大黄 when you mean the sour vegetable.
subtleties: Botanically a vegetable (a leaf stalk), rhubarb is cooked like fruit, with plenty of sugar.

profile.feeling: Crunchy sweet bites in winter; Cantonese dim sum.

senses.def: Chinese water chestnut (Eleocharis dulcis): the crisp, sweet corm

examples.text: 荸荠削了皮，又甜又脆。
examples.tr: Peeled water chestnuts are sweet and crunchy.
examples.py: Bíqi xiāo le pí, yòu tián yòu cuì.

examples.text: 广东的马蹄糕是用荸荠粉做的。
examples.tr: Cantonese water chestnut cake is made with water chestnut starch.
examples.py: Guǎngdōng de mǎtí gāo shì yòng bíqi fěn zuò de.

examples.text: 狮子头里加一点儿荸荠，口感更好。
examples.tr: A little water chestnut makes lion’s-head meatballs nicer to bite.
examples.py: Shīzitóu li jiā yìdiǎnr bíqi, kǒugǎn gèng hǎo.

synonyms.nuance: ‘horse’s hoof’, after the shape: the name in the south and in Cantonese
‘ground pear’: a northern name (also 地梨儿)

etymology.text: From 凫茈 (Middle Chinese bju dzje), the old name in the Compendium of Materia Medica; another theory derives it from 脖脐 ‘navel’, after the navel-like corm (Wiktionary).

funFacts: The ‘water chestnuts’ in Chinese takeaway dishes are this corm: it stays crunchy even when cooked.
English ‘water chestnut’ is also used for 菱角 (water caltrop) — two unrelated plants.
pitfalls: Pronounced bíqi, with a toneless second syllable in standard Mainland speech (Wiktionary also gives bíqí).
It grows in muddy paddies and can carry parasites: wash and peel it well, or cook it.
subtleties: 马蹄 is so common in the south that many Cantonese speakers never say 荸荠.

profile.feeling: Autumn ponds of Jiangnan, boats and picking songs.

senses.def: water caltrop (Trapa): the horned, starchy nut and the floating plant
(Taishanese) spinning top

examples.text: 秋天的江南，人们划船采菱角。
examples.tr: In autumn in Jiangnan, people go out in boats to pick water caltrops.
examples.py: Qiūtiān de Jiāngnán, rénmen huá chuán cǎi língjiao.

examples.text: 煮熟的菱角像栗子一样粉。
examples.tr: Boiled water caltrop is mealy, like chestnut.
examples.py: Zhǔshú de língjiao xiàng lìzi yíyàng fěn.

examples.text: 菱角的壳很硬，两头有尖尖的角。
examples.tr: The shell is hard, with a sharp horn at each end.
examples.py: Língjiao de ké hěn yìng, liǎng tóu yǒu jiānjiān de jiǎo.

collocations.tr: picking water caltrops (a classic image in poetry)

synonyms.nuance: the one-character written word, used in compounds and poetry

etymology.text: 菱 (‘water caltrop’; 艹 ‘plant’ + phonetic 夌 líng) + 角 (‘horn’): the horned caltrop.

funFacts: 菱形 — ‘caltrop shape’ — is the Chinese word for a rhombus or diamond.
English ‘caltrop’ is a spiked weapon scattered against horses; the nut’s horns gave the plant its name.
pitfalls: Standard pinyin is língjiao with a toneless 角 (Wiktionary also gives língjiǎo); 角 alone is jiǎo.
菱 líng sounds like 零, 灵 and 陵 — the 艹 radical tells you it is the plant.
subtleties: In Taishanese 菱角 can also mean a spinning top (Wiktionary).

profile.feeling: Violet desserts and Philippine ube; a tuber of the south.

senses.def: purple yam, ube (Dioscorea alata)

examples.text: 菲律宾人用参薯做紫色的甜点。
examples.tr: Filipinos make purple desserts with purple yam.
examples.py: Fēilǜbīn rén yòng shēnshǔ zuò zǐsè de tiándiǎn.

examples.text: 市场上常把参薯叫作紫山药。
examples.tr: At markets the purple yam is often called “purple shanyao”.
examples.py: Shìchǎng shang cháng bǎ shēnshǔ jiàozuò zǐ shānyao.

examples.text: 参薯可以蒸着吃，也可以煮粥。
examples.tr: Purple yam can be steamed or cooked in congee.
examples.py: Shēnshǔ kěyǐ zhēngzhe chī, yě kěyǐ zhǔ zhōu.

synonyms.nuance: ‘purple Chinese yam’: the everyday market name
‘big tuber’: the name in Taiwan and in Hokkien

etymology.text: 参 (shēn, the 参 of prized roots such as 人参 ‘ginseng’ and 党参) + 薯 (‘tuber, yam’).

funFacts: Ube ice cream and ube cake from the Philippines owe their violet colour to this yam.
pitfalls: 参 is read shēn here (as in 人参), not cān (参加) or cēn (参差).
Not the purple sweet potato 紫薯 (a sweet potato) — and a different species from 山药 (Chinese yam).
subtleties: 参薯 is the dictionary name; in shops you will mostly read 紫山药.

profile.feeling: Crunchy, juicy, slightly sweet — a summer snack of the south.

senses.def: jícama, yam bean (Pachyrhizus erosus): the crisp, juicy tuberous root

examples.text: 豆薯剥了皮可以生吃，像梨一样脆。
examples.tr: Peeled jícama can be eaten raw — crisp like a pear.
examples.py: Dòushǔ bāo le pí kěyǐ shēng chī, xiàng lí yíyàng cuì.

examples.text: 墨西哥人把豆薯切成条，撒上辣椒粉和青柠汁。
examples.tr: Mexicans cut jícama into sticks with chili powder and lime juice.
examples.py: Mòxīgē rén bǎ dòushǔ qiēchéng tiáo, sǎ shang làjiāo fěn hé qīngníng zhī.

examples.text: 豆薯的种子和叶子有毒，只能吃块根。
examples.tr: The seeds and leaves of jícama are poisonous; only the root is eaten.
examples.py: Dòushǔ de zhǒngzi hé yèzi yǒu dú, zhǐ néng chī kuàigēn.

synonyms.nuance: ‘cool tuber’: the name in Beijing and in Guangxi
the Cantonese and Hakka name
the name in Sichuan, Wuhan and Nanjing — but elsewhere 地瓜 is the sweet potato

etymology.text: 豆 (‘bean’) + 薯 (‘tuber’): the ‘bean tuber’ — the plant is a legume with bean-like pods, just as English ‘yam bean’ says.

funFacts: Jícama comes from Nahuatl xicamatl; Spanish galleons carried it from Mexico to the Philippines, and from there it reached China.
pitfalls: 地瓜 means jícama in Sichuan and parts of central China, but the sweet potato in the north and in Taiwan.
subtleties: Briefly cooked it stays crunchy, so it is used like water chestnut in stir-fries.

profile.feeling: Slippery summer greens of the south.

senses.def: Malabar spinach (Basella alba): a climbing vine with thick, slippery leaves eaten as greens

examples.text: 落葵的叶子又厚又滑，炒熟以后黏黏的。
examples.tr: Malabar spinach leaves are thick and slippery, and slimy once cooked.
examples.py: Luòkuí de yèzi yòu hòu yòu huá, chǎoshú yǐhòu niánnián de.

examples.text: 落葵在市场上一般叫木耳菜。
examples.tr: At the market Malabar spinach is usually called mu’ercai.
examples.py: Luòkuí zài shìchǎng shang yìbān jiào mù'ěrcài.

examples.text: 落葵的果实是紫黑色的，可以做染料。
examples.tr: Its berries are purple-black and can be used as a dye.
examples.py: Luòkuí de guǒshí shì zǐhēisè de, kěyǐ zuò rǎnliào.

synonyms.nuance: ‘wood-ear vegetable’, after its slippery texture: the everyday market name in much of the Mainland (Wiktionary marks it regional)
the Cantonese name
‘palace vegetable’: the name in Taiwan

etymology.text: An old book name: 落 + 葵 (the ancient mallow vegetable). Classical names include 蔠葵 and 蘩露 (Wiktionary).

funFacts: In India it is poi, in the Philippines alugbati.
pitfalls: 木耳菜 has nothing to do with 木耳 (wood-ear fungus): the name compares the slippery leaves to it.
In some places 木耳菜 also names a different plant, Gynura cusimbua (Wiktionary).
subtleties: The slime is the same kind of mucilage as in okra (秋葵) — and both names contain 葵.

profile.feeling: Thai soups and Chaoshan braises; a sharp, piney fragrance.

senses.def: galangal: the hard, aromatic rhizome of Alpinia (in cooking mostly greater galangal, Alpinia galanga)

examples.text: 泰国的冬阴功汤里有南姜和香茅。
examples.tr: Thai tom yum soup contains galangal and lemongrass.
examples.py: Tàiguó de dōngyīngōng tāng li yǒu nánjiāng hé xiāngmáo.

examples.text: 南姜比普通的姜硬，香味也不一样。
examples.tr: Galangal is harder than ordinary ginger and smells different.
examples.py: Nánjiāng bǐ pǔtōng de jiāng yìng, xiāngwèi yě bù yíyàng.

examples.text: 潮汕人做卤水离不开南姜。
examples.tr: Chaoshan cooks can’t make their braising liquid without galangal.
examples.py: Cháoshàn rén zuò lǔshuǐ lí bu kāi nánjiāng.

synonyms.nuance: the classic name, used in Chinese medicine; strictly the lesser galangal (Alpinia officinarum)
the botanical name of greater galangal (Alpinia galanga), the Thai kitchen kind

etymology.text: 南 (‘south’) + 姜 (‘ginger’): ‘southern ginger’, a ginger relative of south China and Southeast Asia.

funFacts: English galangal is thought to go back, through Arabic خَلَنْجَان (khalanjān) and Persian, to Chinese 高良姜 — ‘ginger from Gaoliang’, an old place name in Guangdong.
pitfalls: 南姜 is not just ‘southern ginger’: it is a different plant (Alpinia), woody and resinous — don’t swap it 1:1 for 姜.
In a pharmacy, 高良姜 is the lesser galangal, a related but different species.
subtleties: 南姜 is the kitchen name heard in Guangdong and in Thai recipes; 高良姜 is the name in Chinese medicine.

profile.feeling: Bouncy, chewy and almost calorie-free; Sichuan hot pot and diet snacks.

senses.def: konjac (Amorphophallus konjac): the plant and its large corm
konjac food made from the corm’s flour: konjac “tofu”, noodles, jelly

examples.text: 生魔芋有毒，一定要加工以后才能吃。
examples.tr: Raw konjac is toxic; it must be processed before it can be eaten.
examples.py: Shēng móyù yǒu dú, yídìng yào jiāgōng yǐhòu cái néng chī.

examples.text: 魔芋烧鸭是一道有名的川菜。
examples.tr: Duck braised with konjac is a famous Sichuan dish.
examples.py: Móyù shāo yā shì yí dào yǒumíng de chuāncài.

examples.text: 魔芋热量很低，很多人减肥的时候吃。
examples.tr: Konjac is very low in calories; many people eat it when dieting.
examples.py: Móyù rèliàng hěn dī, hěn duō rén jiǎnféi de shíhou chī.

examples.text: 吃火锅的时候我最爱魔芋丝。
examples.tr: At hot pot my favourite is konjac noodles.
examples.py: Chī huǒguō de shíhou wǒ zuì ài móyù sī.

synonyms.nuance: the name in Taiwan and on Japanese-style products (Japanese konnyaku)

etymology.text: 魔 (‘demon, magic’) + 芋 (‘taro’): the ‘demon taro’ — a taro-like corm that is poisonous raw.

funFacts: Its relative the titan arum (Amorphophallus titanum) has one of the largest flowering structures in the world and smells of rotting meat.
Mainland Olympiad slang 蒟蒻 ‘total beginner’ is a pun on 巨弱 ‘very weak’ (Wiktionary).
pitfalls: Konjac jelly mini-cups have caused choking deaths and were banned in the EU — eat konjac jelly in small bites.
subtleties: Its fibre, glucomannan, swells enormously in water; that is what makes konjac foods filling but low in calories.

ref.src: zh.wikipedia: 海蓬子 (title for Salicornia, Wikidata Q159525); Wiktionary has no entry

profile.feeling: Crunchy, salty green shoots from the seaside marsh.

senses.def: glasswort, sea asparagus, marsh samphire (Salicornia): salty, succulent shoots eaten as a sea vegetable

examples.text: 海蓬子长在海边的盐碱地上。
examples.tr: Glasswort grows on salty land by the sea.
examples.py: Hǎipéngzǐ zhǎng zài hǎibiān de yánjiǎndì shang.

examples.text: 海蓬子本身就有咸味，炒的时候不用放盐。
examples.tr: Glasswort is salty by itself — no need to add salt when you stir-fry it.
examples.py: Hǎipéngzǐ běnshēn jiù yǒu xiánwèi, chǎo de shíhou búyòng fàng yán.

examples.text: 江苏沿海有人种海蓬子。
examples.tr: Some people farm glasswort on the Jiangsu coast.
examples.py: Jiāngsū yánhǎi yǒu rén zhòng hǎipéngzǐ.

synonyms.nuance: ‘sea asparagus’: the restaurant name, a loan translation — it is not asparagus
the botanical name (Salicornia europaea; the genus is 盐角草属)

etymology.text: 海 (‘sea’) + 蓬 (a bushy plant, as in 飞蓬 ‘fleabane’) + 子: ‘the bushy plant of the sea’.

funFacts: English ‘glasswort’ comes from its ash, once used to make glass (soda ash).
In Britain it is called marsh samphire.
pitfalls: Not the rock samphire or sea fennel (Crithmum), which English also calls samphire.
subtleties: Promoted in China as a 海洋蔬菜 (sea vegetable) that can be grown on salty coastal land.

profile.feeling: A heat-proof stand-in for spinach, with a seafaring story.

senses.def: New Zealand spinach (Tetragonia tetragonioides)

examples.text: 番杏不怕热，夏天可以代替菠菜。
examples.tr: New Zealand spinach doesn’t mind heat; in summer it can replace spinach.
examples.py: Fānxìng bú pà rè, xiàtiān kěyǐ dàitì bōcài.

examples.text: 番杏最好先焯一下水再炒。
examples.tr: New Zealand spinach is best blanched before stir-frying.
examples.py: Fānxìng zuìhǎo xiān chāo yíxià shuǐ zài chǎo.

examples.text: 库克船长让船员吃番杏，防止坏血病。
examples.tr: Captain Cook had his crew eat New Zealand spinach to prevent scurvy.
examples.py: Kùkè chuánzhǎng ràng chuányuán chī fānxìng, fángzhǐ huàixuèbìng.

synonyms.nuance: ‘New Zealand spinach’: a transparent translation of the English name

etymology.text: 番 (‘foreign’, the prefix of old imports: 番茄, 番薯) + 杏 (‘apricot’).

funFacts: One of very few vegetables from Oceania: Joseph Banks brought it to England after Cook’s first voyage.
pitfalls: 番杏 is a leaf vegetable — nothing to do with apricots (杏).
subtleties: Like spinach it contains oxalic acid; a quick blanch removes much of it.

profile.feeling: Juicy, pear-like crunch — a “new” health fruit.

senses.def: yacón (Smallanthus sonchifolius): the sweet, crunchy tuberous root

examples.text: 雪莲果生吃又甜又脆，像水果一样。
examples.tr: Raw yacón is sweet and crunchy, like a fruit.
examples.py: Xuěliánguǒ shēng chī yòu tián yòu cuì, xiàng shuǐguǒ yíyàng.

examples.text: 雪莲果原产南美的安第斯山区。
examples.tr: Yacón comes from the Andes of South America.
examples.py: Xuěliánguǒ yuánchǎn Nánměi de Āndìsī shānqū.

examples.text: 云南现在种了很多雪莲果。
examples.tr: A lot of yacón is grown in Yunnan now.
examples.py: Yúnnán xiànzài zhòng le hěn duō xuěliánguǒ.

synonyms.nuance: ‘daisy tuber’: the botanical name — the plant is in the sunflower family

etymology.text: A modern name: 雪莲 (‘snow lotus’) + 果 (‘fruit’) — it is neither a lotus nor a fruit, but a root eaten like fruit.

funFacts: Its sweetness comes mostly from fructo-oligosaccharides, which the body hardly digests — so it is low in calories.
pitfalls: 雪莲果 is not 雪莲, the Himalayan snow lotus used in medicine.
subtleties: In the Andes the roots are left in the sun for a few days to make them sweeter.

ref.src: zh.wikipedia: 棕榈心 (title for Wikidata Q743144); Wiktionary has no entry

profile.feeling: Tropical, tender and mild — a salad ingredient from Brazil.

senses.def: heart of palm, palmito: the tender inner core of certain palms

examples.text: 棕榈心常常做成罐头，放在沙拉里。
examples.tr: Heart of palm is usually canned and goes into salads.
examples.py: Zōnglǘxīn chángcháng zuòchéng guàntou, fàng zài shālā li.

examples.text: 巴西是吃棕榈心最多的国家之一。
examples.tr: Brazil is one of the countries that eat the most heart of palm.
examples.py: Bāxī shì chī zōnglǘxīn zuì duō de guójiā zhī yī.

examples.text: 棕榈心又白又嫩，味道有点儿像竹笋。
examples.tr: Heart of palm is white and tender and tastes a little like bamboo shoot.
examples.py: Zōnglǘxīn yòu bái yòu nèn, wèidao yǒudiǎnr xiàng zhúsǔn.

synonyms.nuance: the same word written with 芯 ‘pith, core’

etymology.text: 棕榈 (‘palm tree’) + 心 (‘heart, core’): a loan translation of ‘heart of palm’.

funFacts: Harvesting it kills a single-stemmed palm, so most heart of palm now comes from farmed multi-stemmed palms such as the peach palm.
pitfalls: 榈 is lǘ, with ü — not lú.
subtleties: In China it is an import-shop item, bought in cans or jars.

ref.src: zh.wikipedia: 甘露子 (title for Stachys affinis, Wikidata Q1758702); Wiktionary names it under 地蠶 (“alternative name for 甘露子”) but has no entry of its own

profile.feeling: Crunchy little pagodas in a jar of soy pickles.

senses.def: Chinese artichoke, crosne (Stachys affinis): small, ringed, crunchy tubers

examples.text: 甘露子的样子像一串小螺丝。
examples.tr: Chinese artichokes look like a string of little screws.
examples.py: Gānlùzǐ de yàngzi xiàng yí chuàn xiǎo luósī.

examples.text: 甘露子常常被做成酱菜。
examples.tr: Chinese artichokes are often made into soy-sauce pickles.
examples.py: Gānlùzǐ chángcháng bèi zuòchéng jiàngcài.

examples.text: 法国人把甘露子当作高级蔬菜。
examples.tr: The French treat Chinese artichokes as a luxury vegetable.
examples.py: Fǎguó rén bǎ gānlùzǐ dàngzuò gāojí shūcài.

synonyms.nuance: ‘pagoda vegetable’, after the stacked rings: the common name in pickles and markets (CC-CEDICT)
‘grass stone-silkworm’: an older book name
‘ground silkworm’ (Wiktionary: alternative name for 甘露子)

etymology.text: 甘露 (‘sweet dew’) + 子 (‘small thing’). Its other names — 宝塔 ‘pagoda’, 地蚕 ‘ground silkworm’ — all describe the ringed tubers.

funFacts: French crosne is named after the village of Crosne near Paris, where it was first grown in France in the 1880s.
pitfalls: 宝塔菜 is also heard for romanesco (宝塔花菜) — context decides.
subtleties: The tubers wilt within days of digging, one reason they are mostly sold pickled.

profile.feeling: Summer greens and pink juice soaking into the rice.

senses.def: amaranth greens, edible amaranth (Amaranthus tricolor and relatives)

examples.text: 红苋菜炒出来的汤是粉红色的。
examples.tr: Stir-fried red amaranth gives a pink juice.
examples.py: Hóng xiàncài chǎo chulai de tāng shì fěnhóngsè de.

examples.text: 蒜蓉苋菜是夏天的家常菜。
examples.tr: Amaranth with garlic is a summer home dish.
examples.py: Suànróng xiàncài shì xiàtiān de jiāchángcài.

examples.text: 我买一把苋菜。
examples.tr: I’ll buy a bunch of amaranth.
examples.py: Wǒ mǎi yì bǎ xiàncài.

phrases.text: 六月苋，当鸡蛋；七月苋，金不换
phrases.tr: amaranth in the sixth month is worth eggs; in the seventh, not even gold buys it
phrases.meaning: midsummer amaranth is especially nourishing (folk saying about eating with the season)

synonyms.nuance: the Shanghai and Wu name
the one-character written word

etymology.text: 苋 (traditional 莧, ‘amaranth’: 艹 ‘plant’ + phonetic 见/見) + 菜 (‘vegetable’).

funFacts: Greek ἀμάραντος, the source of ‘amaranth’, means ‘unfading’.
The grain amaranth of the Aztecs belongs to the same genus (苋属).
pitfalls: 苋 (艹 on top) is easy to confuse with 觅 mì ‘to seek’ (爫 on top).
subtleties: Red, green and two-coloured kinds are sold; the red one stains rice pink, which children love.

ref.src: zh.wikipedia: 黄葱 (Allium × proliferum, Wikidata Q41794154), which lists 楼葱 and 楼子葱 as other names; Wiktionary has no entry

profile.feeling: A curious onion that builds little towers.

senses.def: tree onion, Egyptian walking onion (Allium × proliferum): forms clusters of small bulbs on top of the stalk instead of flowers

examples.text: 楼葱的顶上不开花，而是长出一簇小葱头。
examples.tr: The tree onion doesn’t flower on top but grows a cluster of little bulbs.
examples.py: Lóucōng de dǐng shang bù kāi huā, ér shì zhǎngchū yí cù xiǎo cōngtóu.

examples.text: 小葱头落到地上，又长出新的楼葱。
examples.tr: The little bulbs drop to the ground and grow into new tree onions.
examples.py: Xiǎo cōngtóu luòdào dìshang, yòu zhǎngchū xīn de lóucōng.

examples.text: 楼葱的吃法跟大葱差不多。
examples.tr: Tree onions are eaten much like Welsh onions.
examples.py: Lóucōng de chīfǎ gēn dàcōng chàbuduō.

synonyms.nuance: the longer form of the same name
the name under which Chinese Wikipedia files Allium × proliferum
‘dragon-claw onion’, a local name

etymology.text: 楼 (‘storeyed building, tower’) + 葱 (‘scallion’): the bulblets form ‘storeys’ on top of the stalk.

funFacts: English calls it ‘walking onion’: the top-heavy stalk bends over and the bulbs root where they touch the ground.
pitfalls: Not a kind of 大葱: it is a hybrid of the Welsh onion (葱) and a shallot-type onion.
subtleties: A garden curiosity in China (grown here and there, e.g. in Yanbian) rather than a market vegetable.

profile.feeling: Jade-green crunchy sticks from Sichuan kitchens.

senses.def: celtuce, stem lettuce (Lactuca sativa var. augustana): the thick, crisp stem
(dialectal) lettuce

examples.text: 莴笋去皮以后，切丝凉拌很爽口。
examples.tr: Peeled celtuce, cut into shreds and dressed cold, is very refreshing.
examples.py: Wōsǔn qùpí yǐhòu, qiē sī liángbàn hěn shuǎngkǒu.

examples.text: 莴笋叶也能吃，有点儿苦。
examples.tr: Celtuce leaves are edible too, a little bitter.
examples.py: Wōsǔn yè yě néng chī, yǒudiǎnr kǔ.

examples.text: 在四川，莴笋叫青笋。
examples.tr: In Sichuan celtuce is called qingsun.
examples.py: Zài Sìchuān, wōsǔn jiào qīngsǔn.

synonyms.nuance: the general word for the lettuce species; in many northern dialects it means celtuce
‘green shoot’: the Sichuan and Chongqing name

etymology.text: 莴 (as in 莴苣 ‘lettuce’) + 笋 (‘bamboo shoot’): the lettuce whose thick stem is eaten like a shoot.

funFacts: English celtuce (celery + lettuce) was coined by an American seed company in the 20th century.
pitfalls: 莴笋 is not a bamboo shoot (竹笋), despite 笋.
subtleties: Leaves are sold separately as 莴笋叶; the leaf lettuce 油麦菜 is a different vegetable.

profile.feeling: Spring in the mountains, wild greens, bibimbap.

senses.def: fiddleheads: young curled fern fronds (above all bracken) eaten as a vegetable

examples.text: 春天，山里的人上山采蕨菜。
examples.tr: In spring, mountain people go up the hills to pick fiddleheads.
examples.py: Chūntiān, shān li de rén shàng shān cǎi juécài.

examples.text: 韩国拌饭里常常有蕨菜。
examples.tr: Korean bibimbap often contains fiddleheads.
examples.py: Hánguó bànfàn li chángcháng yǒu juécài.

examples.text: 新鲜蕨菜要用开水焯过才能吃。
examples.tr: Fresh fiddleheads must be blanched in boiling water before eating.
examples.py: Xīnxiān juécài yào yòng kāishuǐ chāo guo cái néng chī.

synonyms.nuance: the fern itself; the one-character written word

etymology.text: 蕨 (‘bracken fern’: 艹 ‘plant’ + phonetic 厥 jué) + 菜 (‘vegetable’).

funFacts: In Korean it is gosari (고사리), essential in bibimbap; in Japanese, warabi.
pitfalls: Bracken contains ptaquiloside, a carcinogen: soak and cook it, and eat it in moderation.
subtleties: Dried fiddleheads (干蕨菜) are soaked before cooking, like other dried mountain greens.

ref.src: zh.wikipedia: 油莎草 (Cyperus esculentus, Wikidata Q1165724), “又名油莎豆”; reading of 莎 as suō (‘sedge, Cyperus’) from Wiktionary 莎 and 莎草 suōcǎo; Wiktionary has no entry for the word

profile.feeling: Small wrinkled tubers, sweet and nutty — an oil crop in China.

senses.def: tiger nut, chufa (Cyperus esculentus var. sativus): the small sweet tubers, and the crop

examples.text: 油莎豆是一种莎草的块茎，不是豆子。
examples.tr: Tiger nuts are the tubers of a sedge, not beans.
examples.py: Yóusuōdòu shì yì zhǒng suōcǎo de kuàijīng, bú shì dòuzi.

examples.text: 西班牙瓦伦西亚有一种用油莎豆做的甜饮料。
examples.tr: Valencia in Spain has a sweet drink made from tiger nuts.
examples.py: Xībānyá Wǎlúnxīyà yǒu yì zhǒng yòng yóusuōdòu zuò de tián yǐnliào.

examples.text: 新疆有不少地方种油莎豆，用来榨油。
examples.tr: Quite a few places in Xinjiang grow tiger nuts for oil.
examples.py: Xīnjiāng yǒu bùshǎo dìfang zhòng yóusuōdòu, yònglái zhà yóu.

synonyms.nuance: the plant’s botanical name (‘oil sedge’)
‘iron water chestnut’: a folk name for the hard little tubers

etymology.text: 油 (‘oil’) + 莎 (suō, ‘sedge, Cyperus’, as in 莎草) + 豆 (‘bean’): the oil-rich sedge tuber that looks like a bean.

funFacts: Tiger nuts were eaten in ancient Egypt and have been found in tombs.
Spanish horchata de chufa, from Valencia, is made from them.
pitfalls: 莎 is suō here (as in 莎草 ‘sedge’); shā is only for names and transcriptions such as 莎士比亚.
Not a nut and not a bean, despite English ‘nut’ and Chinese 豆.
subtleties: The wild form, yellow nutsedge, is one of the world’s most troublesome weeds.

absent.reason: Cardoon is not grown or eaten in China and has no established everyday name; Wiktionary gives no Chinese word.
absent.use: Botanical names 刺苞菜蓟 or 大叶菜蓟 (Cynara cardunculus); otherwise described as the wild relative of 洋蓟 (artichoke).

absent.reason: Elephant foot yam is not a common food in China; there is no everyday word and Wiktionary has none.
absent.use: Botanical name 疣柄魔芋 (Amorphophallus paeoniifolius, ‘warty-stalked konjac’); otherwise described as a kind of 魔芋 (konjac).

absent.reason: Garden orache is hardly grown in China; Wiktionary has no Chinese name for it.
absent.use: Botanical name 榆钱菠菜 (Atriplex hortensis, ‘elm-seed spinach’); the genus Atriplex is 滨藜属.

absent.reason: Good King Henry is a European green unknown in China; there is no Chinese word in Wiktionary.
absent.use: Botanical name 菜藜 (Blitum bonus-henricus); otherwise described as 一种欧洲的野菜 ‘a European wild green’ related to 藜 (fat hen).

absent.reason: The Egyptian leek is unknown in China and has no Chinese name.
absent.use: Described as 埃及的一种韭葱 ‘a kind of Egyptian leek’ (韭葱 = leek).

absent.reason: Rock samphire (sea fennel, Crithmum maritimum) is not eaten in China; there is no everyday word and Wiktionary has none.
absent.use: Botanical name 海茴香 (‘sea fennel’). Not to be confused with glasswort, 海蓬子, which English also calls samphire.

absent.reason: Oca is an Andean tuber unknown in Chinese markets; Wiktionary has no Chinese word.
absent.use: Botanical names 块茎酢浆草 (‘tuberous wood sorrel’) or 酢浆薯; otherwise 南美的一种块茎 ‘a South American tuber’.

absent.reason: Mashua is an Andean tuber unknown in China; Wiktionary has no Chinese word.
absent.use: Botanical name 块茎金莲花 (‘tuberous nasturtium’) — a relative of the garden nasturtium 旱金莲.

absent.reason: Salsify is practically unknown as a vegetable in China; Wiktionary has no Chinese name.
absent.use: Botanical name 蒜叶婆罗门参 (Tragopogon porrifolius); the genus Tragopogon is 婆罗门参属.

absent.reason: Skirret is an old European root vegetable unknown in China; neither Wiktionary nor Chinese Wikipedia has a Chinese name.
absent.use: Described as 一种欧洲的根菜 ‘a European root vegetable’; it belongs to the water-parsnip genus Sium (泽芹属).

absent.reason: Arracacha is an Andean root crop unknown in China; Wiktionary has no Chinese word.
absent.use: Sometimes described as 秘鲁胡萝卜 ‘Peruvian carrot’ (a translation of an English nickname), or by its Latin name Arracacia.

absent.reason: Land cress (Barbarea verna) is not grown in China; there is no Chinese word.
absent.use: Described as 一种像西洋菜的野菜 ‘a wild green like watercress’; the genus Barbarea is 山芥属.

absent.reason: Ramps (Allium tricoccum) are a North American wild leek not found in China; there is no established word.
absent.use: Described as 北美野韭 ‘North American wild leek’ (the Wikidata label); compare 熊葱 (European wild garlic), a close relative.

absent.reason: Pearl onions are rarely sold in China; there is no established word and Wiktionary has none.
absent.use: Recipes translate it as 珍珠洋葱 ‘pearl onion’ or simply say 小洋葱 ‘small onions’.

absent.reason: Elephant garlic is rare in China and has no established everyday word; Wiktionary has none.
absent.use: Encyclopedias call it 象大蒜 (‘elephant garlic’, a translation); botanically it is a kind of leek (韭葱, Allium ampeloprasum), not true garlic.

absent.reason: Root (Hamburg) parsley is practically unknown in China; there is no Chinese word.
absent.use: Described with 欧芹 (parsley): 一种吃根的欧芹 ‘a parsley grown for its root’.
